Research task for Nxeon (VPS/game-hosting business). We're building NxLabs, a mod/plugin catalog covering all games we host. Earlier research this session already covered ~29 of our 46 hosted game families (Minecraft via Modrinth, CS2 via GitHub, Rust via uMod/Oxide, Steam-Workshop-config-write games, mod.io games, etc.) — real API-based research only, citing live endpoints, confirming license fields, no assumptions.

You're covering 8 of the remaining un-researched games we currently offer hosting for: **palworld**, **bedrock** (Minecraft Bedrock Edition — NOT Java, a genuinely separate modding ecosystem), **schedule1** (a smaller/newer indie game — verify it's even real and currently popular before assuming), and four Plutonium-launcher classic Call of Duty titles: **plutoniumt4** (World at War), **plutoniumt5** (Black Ops), **plutoniumt6** (Black Ops 2), **plutoniumiw5** (Modern Warfare 3) — these run through the third-party "Plutonium" project (plutonium.pw), which revives dedicated-server support for these old, officially-abandoned CoD titles.

For EACH, determine and report:

**Palworld**: Real primary mod distribution channel — I believe it's predominantly Nexus Mods plus a UE4SS (Unreal Engine 4/5 Scripting System) mod-loader ecosystem, NOT Steam Workshop (verify this — does Palworld actually have Steam Workshop support or not?). If Nexus is primary, flag as excluded per existing policy (AUP bars mass-fetch+rehost). Check if there's any secondary channel (GitHub topic search for `palworld-mod`, mod.io presence) with better legal terms.

**Bedrock**: This is a completely different modding format from Java Minecraft — "Add-Ons" (behavior packs/resource packs, .mcpack/.mcaddon files), historically distributed via community sites like mcpedl.com (Minecraft PE DL) rather than an official store for servers. Determine: (a) does mcpedl.com have any API or is it scrape-only with unclear ToS (find and read their actual terms/robots.txt), (b) is there any other real distribution channel with an API and clearer license posture (GitHub topic search for `bedrock-addon`/`minecraft-bedrock-addon` is worth trying), (c) do Bedrock DEDICATED SERVERS (BDS, what Nxeon actually hosts) even support installing Add-Ons server-side in a way relevant to a hosting company, or are Add-Ons mostly a client-side/Realms concept — this matters a lot for whether this is even a relevant feature to build.

**Schedule 1**: First confirm this is a real, current game with real player population and any dedicated-server/modding support at all (it's less well-known than the rest of our catalog — don't assume, verify). If it has real mod support, find the actual channel (Steam Workshop, Nexus, Thunderstore, GitHub) the same way as other research this session.

**Plutonium (t4/t5/t6/iw5)**: These are NOT standard Steam-hosted dedicated servers — Plutonium is a separate community project (plutonium.pw) that provides its own client/server binaries and its own custom-map/mod ecosystem for these old CoD titles (since the original anti-cheat/matchmaking is dead). Determine: (a) does Plutonium have any real API for browsing/fetching custom maps or mods, or is distribution purely via their own forums/Discord/website with no API, (b) what are Plutonium's own terms of service around building tooling/products on top of their project — read their actual ToS/rules if published, (c) is there a real GitHub-based mod scene for any of these titles (topic search per title) as an alternative.

Be concise and evidence-based — real URLs, real fetched pages/API responses, explicit "not found"/"scrape-only, no API" when that's the honest answer rather than padding with assumption. Under 500 words in your final report, plus short real evidence snippets where useful.

**Palworld** — Steam Workshop IS real (added in the 1.0 "Home Sweet Home" update), confirmed via https://steamcommunity.com/app/1623730/workshop/ and Steam news. But it's officially labeled *experimental*, Windows-dedicated-server only, and the majority of the ecosystem still runs through Nexus Mods (3,615+ mods) via the UE4SS scripting loader — Nexus stays excluded per this session's existing AUP policy (mass-fetch+rehost barred). **Recommended channel: Steam Workshop API** (same integration pattern already used for other Workshop-config-write games this session) — it's the one channel with clean legal terms and programmatic access. Secondary options checked and rejected: mod.io has no real Palworld presence (only unrelated cross-game reskins), Thunderstore has a Palworld community but is secondary to Steam Workshop/Nexus. GitHub topic search (`palworld-mod`, `palworld`) surfaces only individual dev repos/toolkits, not a distribution API.

**Bedrock** — mcpedl.com robots.txt (https://mcpedl.com/robots.txt) only blocks `/go/`, `/leaving/`, `/admin/`, `/dashboard/` — technically crawlable, but their Terms of Use (https://mcpedl.com/terms/) explicitly prohibit redistribution, systematic data extraction, and "sidestepping regular interfaces" — **scrape-only, no API, ToS-hostile to a mass-fetch product**. No official/documented API found (the one "API docs" hit, docs.better-mcpedl.net, is an unofficial third party, unverified). GitHub topic search (`bedrock-addon`, `minecraft-bedrock-addon`) found real repos but they're dev tools/templates (Mojang's own `bedrock-samples`, addon-maker GUIs), not a catalog/distribution API. Most importantly: **Behavior Packs are genuinely server-side** on BDS (loaded via `world_behavior_packs.json`/`world_resource_packs.json` with manifest UUIDs) — this is directly relevant to a hosting company, unlike Resource Packs which are client-only. Recommendation: this is a legitimate feature to build, but with no clean bulk-content API, it would have to be manual-upload (customer supplies .mcpack) rather than a browsable catalog like other games.

**Schedule I** — Confirmed real and currently popular: Steam appid 3164500, ~11,200 avg daily players over the last 30 days, historical peak 459,075 (steamdb.info/app/3164500). Has a real dedicated server mode. Mod loader is **MelonLoader** (Unity Il2Cpp/Mono loader), with mods split across **Nexus Mods** (excluded, AUP) and **Thunderstore** (https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/) — Thunderstore is the same clean-API/clear-license channel already used for other MelonLoader-based games this session. **Recommended: Thunderstore API**, same as prior precedent. No official Steam Workshop integration exists.

**Plutonium (t4/t5/t6/iw5)** — No official API of any kind found. Distribution of custom maps/mods is entirely via the Plutonium forum (forum.plutonium.pw) and MEGA/Discord links — confirmed "no API, forum/manual-download only" via multiple searches for map/mod endpoints.
